data.title: Why Southern Copper's Strong Quarter Could Steer Investors To ETFs
data.description:
You can own Southern Copper directly, or you can hold it as one slice of a broader fund. Holding just the single stock means living with company specific issues from Simply Wall St such as an unstable dividend track record, or the risk that profitability and free cash flow may not stay at recent levels. Owning Southern Copper inside a fund spreads those business specific swings across other holdings, and also dilutes both the downside and the upside that comes from this one miner.

Fresh results give you something concrete to weigh here. On 25 November 2026, Southern Copper reported third quarter net sales of US$4.7b and raised its copper production outlook for 2026 to 918,000 tonnes, which points to a busier future for its mines and smelters. That update, plus the new cash and stock dividend, is what you would be plugging into your portfolio if you owned shares directly or through EPU, COPX or ICOP.

Would you rather build your own basket around Southern Copper? Explore 16 top copper producer stocks.

iShares MSCI Peru and Global Exposure ETF (EPU)

Credicorp leads this portfolio and pulls a lot of EPU toward Peruvian banking and financial services, rather than metals alone. Gold producers such as Compañía de Minas Buenaventura add another slice of mining alongside copper. Southern Copper is still a major piece of what you own. It sits as the second largest holding at 21.45% of the fund, so each US$1,000 in EPU puts about US$214 into Southern Copper and the rest into other Peru linked businesses across banks, gold and broader metals.

Southern Copper’s unstable dividend record is one clear risk if you only hold the stock. EPU keeps that company specific issue in check by pairing the miner with large financial holdings like Credicorp, whose earnings and payouts lean on banking and credit demand rather than copper markets. The rest of the mix across diversified metals and distributors means this ETF gives you Southern Copper plus exposure to banks, gold and other industries that the stock alone cannot provide.

Not every stock inside EPU is priced the same way. Find out how many of EPU's holdings look undervalued.

Global X Copper Miners ETF (COPX)

COPX keeps Southern Copper to 4.5% of the portfolio, so each US$1,000 only puts about US$45 into this one miner and leaves most of your result driven by other holdings. The mix is heavy on Diversified Metals and Mining at 52.4% and Copper at 43.9%, with a small slice in Gold. BHP Group and Boliden together hold a noticeable share at the top, which steers a lot of the copper and broader mining exposure even though no single stock dominates the fund.

One risk around Southern Copper is that higher copper volumes could help keep revenue and earnings firmer than a very cautious share price view allows. COPX still revolves around copper and diversified miners, so that kind of surprise in the metal and its producers would echo across many of its holdings, which leaves you less exposed to Southern Copper alone but not insulated from how copper mining as a whole performs.

See how COPX's returns compare with the market, from one week to five years

iShares Copper and Metals Mining ETF (ICOP)

COPX and ICOP hold a similar slice of Southern Copper, with ICOP putting 4.65% of its money into the miner, so each US$1,000 means roughly US$46 tied to this one stock and the rest driven by other positions. ICOP leans on Diversified Metals and Mining at 48.1%, Copper at 36.1% and Gold at 12.2%. Anglo American and Grupo México de together hold 17.9% of the fund, which pulls more of your outcome toward large global miners that COPX does not emphasise as heavily, even though about 59% of ICOP overlaps COPX.

One risk with Southern Copper is that current profitability and free cash flow might not be unusually high after all, which would challenge any thesis built on those numbers fading. ICOP holds a wider mix of producers, so any reassessment of profit sustainability at Southern Copper alone is softened by Anglo American, Grupo México de and others that depend on different mine sets and regions. You are still heavily tied to metals and mining though, so your result depends on how this broader group of miners handles its own costs and copper demand over time.

See what you'd actually own if you bought ICOP, from its 80 positions to how much sits in the top 10.

Choosing your Southern Copper exposure

Think about what you want Southern Copper to be inside your portfolio. EPU makes it a central bet. Around US$1,000 in EPU means roughly US$214 in the miner, plus a heavy tilt to Peruvian banks and a fee of US$59 a year on a US$10,000 investment. COPX and ICOP treat Southern Copper more as a supporting position at about US$45 to US$46 per US$1,000, with the real choice between them being breadth and cost.

COPX is more concentrated at 47 holdings and charges US$65 on US$10,000. ICOP owns 80 stocks and is cheapest at US$47. After those strong recent results, you decide whether you want Southern Copper mostly paired with banks or with a wider group of miners, and how comfortable you are with an uneven stream of dividends along the way.

Credicorp alone makes up 25.17% of EPU, so how it's priced matters to anyone holding the fund. Check whether Credicorp trades above or below its fair value.

data.title: How a Small Potash Developer Jumped A Massive Hurdle in Saskatchewan
data.description:
Key points

  • Buffalo Potash has connected all three horizontal wells underground at its Disley Project in Saskatchewan, proving its patented extraction design works in practice.

  • By showing fluid can reliably move between wells, Buffalo has cleared the prime technical risk that kept it trading at a discount to conventional potash miners.

  • The next step is pumping potash-rich brine to the surface ahead of a targeted Q1 2027 production start, though the project is still advancing without a formal feasibility study.

If you look at the world’s major potash mines, almost all of them belong to the major players like Mosaic (NYSE:MOS) or K+S. That’s not coincidental. Extracting potash traditionally requires sinking vertical wells and billions of dollars in infrastructure. 

That expenditure is typically a barrier to entry that’s kept smaller players on the sidelines. 

Buffalo Potash (TSXV:BUFF) is trying to rewrite the playbook on a prime patch of land in the middle of Saskatchewan. A plot that happens to border Mosaic’s Belle Plaine mine and K+S’ Bethune operation. Instead of drilling straight down with expensive vertical wells, Buffalo opted to lay three 565-meter horizontal wells along the base of the deposit. Essentially, one central injector flanked by two producers. 

Until this week, that exact setup was one of the reasons investors were staying cautious. Using horizontal wells to dissolve potash underground is the new kid on the block. 

Buffalo patented it and dubbed it the “Horizontal Line-Drive” (HLD) method, which has never proven its mettle at this scale. Mostly due to the fact that if the salty water pumped down doesn’t reliably reach the outer wells, the whole model is kaput. 

Question quelled

That question was just answered. Following its first well connection on November 23, Buffalo confirmed on the 25th that it’s connected the second producer well, completing an underground loop across all three wells. They’ve also reported pressure and fluid readings matching the subsurface engineering model predictions.

“Connecting the second producer well gives us confidence that what we're seeing underground is repeatable, which is exactly what we set out to demonstrate at this stage," CEO Steve Halabura said, noting the team is now laser-focused on delivering brine to the surface. 

For the investors 

So, what happens next (and why does it matter)? Simply put, Buffalo has cleared the engineering hurdle that often snags other runners. From here on, the process relies on the same solution-mining principles used across the region for 60 years which is to circulate brine, dissolve the potash and pump the mineral-rich liquid up for processing. 

Before it sees sunlight however, engineers will use an 11-stage packer system. Sounds complicated, but it’s essentially just a series of adjustable internal seals along the wells that pressurize different sections and widen the flow underground. 

This is also known as the Mining Plane.

Disley: by the numbers

Quick note: Economic figures come from Buffalo’s May 2026 Preliminary Economic Assessment. All the details can be found in Buffalo’s November 25 release.

What it all means

For investors, the broader story is the proof in the method’s pudding and how the tech can potentially shift Buffalo’s valuation narrative seeing as horizontal solution mining is designed to deliver lower operating costs and a smaller environmental footprint. 

Successfully proving it works at the Initial Production Module (IPM) gives Buffalo a repeatable, low-CapEx blueprint to build on. 

Once the company hits first production, still targeted for Q1 2027, the IP will be proven for deployment across other spaces at Disley, which can handily lead to scaling to a 1.125 million-metric-ton-per-year target.

What could still go wrong?

There is still plenty of executional risk between an underground connection and commercial cash flow. Buffalo is advancing the starter plant based on assessments rather than formal mineral feasibility reports. This means the real-world recoveries, costs and timelines can still vary wildly. They’re also working to finalize a royalty deal with Altius Royalty Corporation (announced October 22) to fund the remaining site and surface processing build-out. 

This article was written independently by the author, without issuer input or approval. Buffalo Potash has a marketing services agreement with Simply Wall St. Details on compensation and other important information can be found in the disclosure and disclaimer at the end of this narrative.

Technical and scientific information in this article is drawn from Buffalo Potash Corp’s news release dated November 25, 2026, which was reviewed and approved by independent Qualified Person Jared Galenzoski, P.Geo., FIMMM, in accordance with National Instrument 43-101. Readers should note that no mineral reserves have been established at the Disley Project, the company’s decision to advance the Initial Production Module is based on a Preliminary Economic Assessment rather than a feasibility study, and its Horizontal Line-Drive mining method has not yet been operated at commercial scale.

data.title: Why You Might Be Interested In Shore Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ:SHBI) For Its Upcoming Dividend

Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that Shore Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ:SHBI) is about to go ex-dividend in just four days. The ex-dividend date occurs one day before the record date, which is the day on which shareholders need to be on the company's books in order to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. In the past 10 years, Shore Bancshares has increased its dividend at approximately 17% a year on average. It's exciting to see that both earnings and dividends per share have grown rapidly over the past few years.

Final Takeaway

Is Shore Bancshares an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? When companies are growing rapidly and retaining a majority of the profits within the business, it's usually a sign that reinvesting earnings creates more value than paying dividends to shareholders. data.description:
• Pan American Silver reported past exploration results from the La Colorada mine in Mexico, including the high grade Elena, Denisse, Catalina and Filomena veins, plus the La Chona Breccia, with detailed drill intercepts and channel samples across multiple underground levels.
  • The La Chona Breccia and new high grade veins could influence how Pan American Silver weighs narrow but rich structures against wider, lower grade zones that may suit bulk mining methods, each with different cost and development trade offs.
  • We will examine how Pan American Silver's investment narrative is affected by the new high grade Elena vein discovery at La Colorada.

Pan American Silver Investment Narrative Recap

To own Pan American Silver, you need to be comfortable with a miner that leans heavily on La Colorada and a pipeline of long life silver and gold districts. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St centres on La Colorada Skarn and Timmins delivering over time while higher cost gold operations and Jacobina issues are managed. The fresh vein results at La Colorada add geological interest but do not change that core thesis on their own.

In the near term, the key swing factor is execution on La Colorada Skarn and related high grade zones without cost or schedule setbacks that would strain the roughly US$3.4b liquidity pool. The biggest risk remains operational underperformance in the gold segment and prolonged constraints at Jacobina, which could tighten cash generation just as growth projects require heavy investment.

The latest La Colorada vein update slots directly into one of the main catalysts in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, which highlights expanding inferred resources and new structures such as Elena and Filomena as a support for future mine inventory. Fresh drill intercepts and channel samples from Elena, Denisse, Catalina and Filomena plus La Chona Breccia give that storyline more technical detail.

For you, the practical question is whether Pan American Silver can turn these narrow but very high grade veins and the wider La Chona Breccia into a coherent mine plan that feeds the Skarn concept and near term mill schedules. Execution risk sits around integrating these zones, maintaining metallurgical performance in line with testing, and doing so while gold operations, Jacobina remediation and large capex at La Colorada Skarn and Timmins are all competing for capital and management focus.

What The La Colorada Veins Mean For Pan American Silver's Numbers

Pan American Silver's narrative projects $4.8 billion revenue and $1.8 billion earnings by 2029. This aligns with analysts assuming 2.2% yearly revenue growth and implies a $200 million earnings increase from $1.6 billion today.

data.title: Plug Power (PLUG) Stock Still Looks Pricey As Shares Fell 97%
data.description:
Plug Power trades near US$1.07 a share after a long slide, and the question now is whether that price can be supported by what the company actually generates in sales. Recent news around large electrolyzer projects has put fresh attention on the stock, but the real issue for you as an investor is how those contracts stack up against the revenue base that is already in place.

  • Over the past 5 years, Plug Power shareholders have seen the stock fall 96.8%. This puts the focus firmly on whether the current valuation can still be explained by its sales profile.
  • The launch of the GenEco Scale electrolyzer platform and projects like Arcadia eFuels’ planned 280 MW plant in Texas may support expectations for higher hydrogen related revenue over time. This matters directly for how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of Plug Power’s sales.

Does Plug Power Look Pricey on Sales?

P/S works reasonably well for Plug Power because investors are currently focused more on potential revenue tied to hydrogen projects than on near term profits. The stock trades on a P/S of about 1.9x, which sits above the electrical industry average near 1.6x and also above the peer group around 1.8x.

The Fair Ratio model, which adjusts the benchmark P/S for Plug Power’s own growth outlook, margins, size and risk profile, indicates that the shares appear overvalued on this yardstick.
